title: earlier-lifecycle-check-reused-at-later-material-stage

proposition.statement: A relying system must not treat lifecycle state established at an earlier composition stage as sufficient evidence of lifecycle state at a later material authorization or execution boundary when relevant state may have changed.

preconditions: Lifecycle or status is evaluated at issuance, discovery, presentation, or an earlier authorization stage.
A later material stage is reached after time has passed or another component has acted.
Revocation, suspension, expiry, authority state, or applicable policy could have changed between the two stages.
No freshness or re-evaluation rule positively establishes continuity.

trigger.statement: The later component reuses the earlier lifecycle result and returns PASS without obtaining current-enough evidence for the later material boundary.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence of lifecycle state at the later material stage.
Evidence distinguishing the earlier evaluation time from the later material decision or execution time.
Evidence that the lifecycle observation is current enough for the later decision.
Evidence describing which stage performed the earlier check and which stage relies on it later.

falsification.condition: The system returns PASS at execution using only an earlier lifecycle check when intervening state change is possible and continuity is unproved.
A stale earlier-stage status result is treated as equivalent to a later-stage current-state evaluation.

references.note: Repository judgment record for this failure proposition.
